subject: Runway smoothing: voucher split vs top-up — next steps
messages:
From: Anjali Rao <anjali@helionai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dave Chen <davec@helionai.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Runway smoothing: voucher split vs top-up — need clarity

Priyom,

Thanks for the demo earlier this week — the team is impressed with the latency and the KV-caching behavior on our RAG workloads. We have a short funding runway and the execs want a clean way to keep the POC running through the end of Q3 without committing to a long-term reserved contract yet.

Two procurement asks that need to be resolved this week so we can keep engineering running: 
- Can we do a small voucher top-up that extends the pilot by 6 weeks and converts unused portion into credits for conversion?
- Alternatively, can we split the voucher now (50/50) so part covers the next 6 weeks and part is claimable later as flexible credits? Procurement hates timeboxes that can’t convert.

Also: what’s the net effect on price if we convert to a 6-month committed seat/units agreement in mid-July — roughly what discount should we expect if we make the conversion before the voucher expires?

I’ve attached a short summary of the current usage and forecasts. Procurement will be on standby: procurements@helionai.com.

Can you outline the mechanics and confirm any paperwork we need?

—Anjali

Attachments: Helion_Runway_Proposal_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Anjali Rao <anjali@helionai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runway smoothing: voucher split vs top-up — need clarity

Anjali — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the usage snapshot. Quick answers up front, then a recommended path.

Short answers: 
- Voucher top-up: yes, we can add a time-box top-up (6 weeks) and allow unused tokens to be converted to a credit balance usable against a committed conversion within 90 days of top-up expiry.
- Voucher split: we can structure a 50/50 split at purchase time where the secondary bucket is converted into a flexible credit voucher (expires in 6 months). This adds a small admin fee.
- Conversion discount: if you convert to a 6-month commit before the top-up/voucher expiry, we can offer a conversion credit plus a 12% committed discount off list on the recurring unit price (this is our standard mid-pilot conversion incentive).

Recommended path (min friction): purchase a modest top-up that keeps the pilot live for 6 weeks while we finalize procurement and use that period to decide on conversion. The top-up converts unused to credits automatically if you elect to convert within 90 days — no extra paperwork beyond the PO and a brief amendment. If procurement needs predictable accounting treatment, go with the split and we’ll generate a voucher that shows as deferred credit on your books.

Next steps I propose: 
1) I’ll send a short amendment + invoice template for the 6-week top-up (no legal redlines required).
2) Marcus will confirm the exact token/hour estimate for the top-up so we size it correctly (keeping 20% buffer for burst tests).
3) Laura can coordinate the PO flow and provide the accounting-friendly voucher language if needed.

I attached a clean proposal (Helion_Runway_Proposal_v2.pdf) and a draft SOW for procurement to review. Happy to jump on a 30-min call with procurement and finance tomorrow.

Best,
Priyom
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW-Helion-PO.docx
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Anjali Rao <anjali@helionai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runway smoothing: voucher split vs top-up — sizing notes

Anjali — I dug into the telemetry you sent and modeled two options: top-up (6 weeks) vs split. Key points below: 

Top-up (recommended conservative size):
- Estimated consumption: 18M gen tokens + 2.5M emb tokens over 6 weeks based on current pacing.
- Buffer: add 20% (~4M gen tokens) to avoid throttling during feature tests.
- Outcome: unused tokens auto-creditable if you convert within 90 days.

Split voucher (procurement-friendly):
- Structure: 50% active (immediately available), 50% parked as flexible credit voucher (6-month redemption window).
- Admin fee: one-time 3% (to cover accounting adjustments and voucher administration).
- Benefit: clearer for finance — shows as prepaid/deferrable.

Cost delta: the split option increases effective unit price by ~2.8% compared to a pure top-up (because of the admin fee and shorter time-to-convert assumptions). If you plan to convert to a commit in July, that delta is typically recovered by the committed discount and/or conversion credit.

If you want I can produce an exact token-level invoice for both structures by EOD Monday.

—Marcus (Sales Engineering)
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Anjali Rao <anjali@helionai.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, procurements@helionai.com
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 16:44:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Runway smoothing: voucher split vs top-up — next steps

Thanks team — quick update after talking to finance and procurement at Helion: procurement prefers the split to keep Q2 spend tidy, but finance asked if we can waive the admin fee if they sign a PO for the split today and include conversion within 60 days (instead of 90).

Our response options: 
A) Waive admin fee if PO signed today + include 60-day conversion window, with standard 12% early-conversion discount retained.
B) Keep 3% admin fee but offer an incremental 3% conversion credit applied if they convert within 45 days.

Action items: 
- Priyom: confirm approval for option A (waive admin fee) or B (credit) with revenue ops.
- Marcus: prep final invoice numbers for both options (token counts and unit prices).
- Laura: prep amendment language for the split voucher and PO-friendly phrasing.

Anjali — if you can get procurement to do the PO today, we’ll fast-track the paperwork and provision the split voucher so engineering can run without interruption. Happy to hop on a brief call to close.

—Priyom
